W-01.why: Gloss set for 'temperate'. Primary sense (mild climate) is the trap; 'lukewarm' is really tepid; 'abstaining' is the rare-but-real sense. SAT tests the restraint sense -> measured. Paired with W-02.

W-02.why: Same headword 'temperate' as W-01, richer glosses. 'Slow to reach a verdict' is not a sense at all; climate is primary/trap. Moderate and restrained matches W-01's 'measured'.

W-03.why: No channel fires. Weak odd-one-out: reversible is the only non-manner/non-cause term.

W-04.why: Gloss set for 'economy'. 'System of trade' is the primary trap; 'household management' is the etymology trap; 'low cost' is attributive. Tested sense is economy = sparing use of means.

W-05.why: 'generous' is a throwaway; among the three epistemic options the hedged/qualified one is the key (hedging channel). Incontrovertible is too absolute for a WiC key.

W-06.why: Gloss set for 'color'. Literal pigment sense is primary trap; SAT tests the figurative 'color one's judgment' = bias the impression of.

W-07.why: Register channel: 'dispositive' is the technical/legal outlier in a set of ordinary adjectives.

W-08.why: Register channel: 'coeval' is the rarest word in the set. Held deliberately against the pull of 'conjectural' to test the channel.

W-09.why: Specificity channel: 'verbatim transcripts' is the most precise/technical. Conflicts with the hedging channel, which would pick 'provisional drafts' - recorded as a channel collision.

W-10.why: Gloss set for 'address'. Residence is primary trap, 'formal speech' is the well-known secondary, 'directing a letter' is the verb sense. Rarest live sense = adroitness/skill in handling situations.

W-11.why: Gloss set for 'homely'. US-common 'plain and unadorned' is the trap; the older/British homelike sense is the tested one. Between A and C, A is the idiomatic gloss.

W-12.why: Only option that is a literal sense of a plausible single headword (accretions/accumulations); the other three are drawn from unrelated families (money, insight, ornament).

W-13.why: Odd-one-out: chronicle/instruct/publicize are all outward communication acts; 'discern' is perception. Singleton taken as key per the three-distractors-from-one-family pattern.

W-14.why: Cross-item pairing: this is the terse partner of W-04 (headword 'economy'). machinery = the trade-system gloss, prosperity = the wealth gloss, frugality = the financial-thrift gloss; spareness is the stylistic sparing-use sense that W-04 keys.

W-15.why: premature/incomplete/unwarranted all mean insufficiently supported and are near-interchangeable in most slots, so none can be a unique key; 'circular' is the one specific, non-substitutable term.

W-16.why: Odd-one-out: concession/maneuver/oversight are all strategic-or-error framings; 'a genuine prediction' is the lone sincere reading and the only one 'genuine' marks as unhedged.

W-17.why: Near-synonym elimination: accommodation and negotiation are interchangeable compromise terms, so neither is a unique key. Of the remaining two, 'imposition' is the unilateral odd-one-out; 'open rivalry' also breaks the one-word format.

W-18.why: Collocation/specificity in translation discourse: exacting/faithful are a near-synonym pair; literal is the standard foil for idiomatic; 'idiomatic' is the technical term of art.

W-19.why: Parallel-pair elimination: 'an act of candor'/'an act of contrition' share a frame and cancel; of the two survivors, 'a bid for prestige' is the motive-shaped one, 'a lapse in judgment' the generic throwaway.

W-20.why: No channel fires cleanly; all four are same-register formal adjectives with no shared family. Defaulted to the ambiguity term.
